chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-A'lawi from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan from his grandfather from Ali ibn Ja'far from his father from their forefathers from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the Ansar, from the Banu al-Najjar, came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'I pronounced Zihar with my wife and then had intercourse with her before expiating.' He asked: 'What drove you to do that?' He said: 'I saw the glint of her anklet and the whiteness of her shins in the moonlight, so I had intercourse with her.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not approach her until you expiate,' and he ordered him to perform the expiation of Zihar and to seek forgiveness from Allah.

Thus, there is nothing in it that contradicts what we have previously stated regarding the obligation of two expiations after intercourse, because what is in the report is that he ordered him to perform the expiation of Zihar, and it does not state that he ordered him to perform one expiation or two. If this is possible, then there is no contradiction between the reports. Furthermore, if it were explicit that he was obligated to perform only one expiation, we would interpret it as applying to the one who did it out of ignorance, because for the one whose ruling is that he owes one expiation, this indicates what was narrated.

key_terms.الظِّهَار: Zihar: A pre-Islamic form of divorce where a man declares his wife to his back/mother, requiring expiation.
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَة: Kaffarah: Expiation or atonement for a specific act or sin.
key_terms.بَنِي النَّجَّار: Banu al-Najjar: A prominent clan of the Ansar in Medina.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiation when a man pronounces Zihar and then has intercourse before expiating?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, an Ansari man from Banu al-Najjar committed Zihar and then had intercourse with his wife before expiation, prompting the Prophet to order both the specific expiation for Zihar and general repentance. Al-Tusi’s juristic analysis clarifies that mentioning the Zihar expiation does not negate the obligation of the separate expiation for intercourse, as the text is not exclusive. This supports the Shia view that the two expiations are distinct obligations, though the report may also accommodate the case of one who acted in ignorance.
